jurisdiction: City of Zurich, canton of Zurich, Switzerland
language_note: Most underlying Swiss sources are published in German. The federal tariff is multilingual.

social_security.excludes: Occupational pension (BVG) and accident insurance, as instructed by the assignment pack.

insurance_premiums.assumption: Qualifying premiums after subsidies are sufficient to use the full single-person cap, with pillar 2 or 3a contributions made. These are capped deductions, not automatic allowances.

excluded: Actual occupational pension (BVG) and accident insurance contributions
Debt interest, donations, dependants and other individual deductions

rounding.note: Federal taxable income is rounded down to CHF 100 under the published tariff. The same rounding is applied to the Zurich tax base in this model.

federal_tariff.name: Grundtarif (single person), direct federal tax
federal_tariff.description: Select the greatest lower threshold not exceeding taxable income. Tax is the base at that threshold plus the marginal rate applied to the excess.

cantonal_simple_tax_tariff.name: Grundtarif (single person), einfache Staatssteuer
cantonal_simple_tax_tariff.description: The simple tax is an intermediate figure. It is calculated once and multiplied by each multiplier.

excluded_from_model: Personal tax (CHF 24 in the city of Zurich)

calculator_check.tool: ESTV income and wealth tax calculator, version 2.1.3

matching_tax_base_run.inputs: Tax year 2026, municipality 8001 Zurich, single, no children, no church affiliation, zero wealth, taxable income supplied directly as CHF 152,400 cantonal and CHF 153,500 federal

gross_income_run.inputs: Same, but gross employment income of CHF 170,000 with the calculator's own default deductions
gross_income_run.note: The calculator additionally deducted occupational pension and accident insurance contributions, which this model excludes on the pack's instruction. The model is about 7.7% higher as a result.
